title: Pathology: basal cell and squamous cell carcinoma of the skin

header.contentArea: Pathology: non-melanoma skin cancer (clinical and histology findings)
guidelineVersions: BAD guidelines for basal cell carcinoma 2021 (Nasr et al., Br J Dermatol 2021)
BAD guidelines for cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma 2020 (Keohane et al., Br J Dermatol 2021)
NICE NG12 Suspected cancer: recognition and referral (published June 2015, last updated 15 April 2026)

related.why: Melanoma: the same skin cancer clinic, with Breslow staging and margins
The excision itself: planning an ellipse and closing it

brief.scenario: Mrs Isla Buchanan, 70, is a retired farmer with fair skin. She has a 1 cm lesion on the ala of her nose and a 1.5 cm lesion on her bald scalp, both present for several months. Written findings: the nasal lesion is a 1 cm shiny, pearly, skin-coloured nodule with a raised, rolled edge and fine branching vessels running over its surface. The scalp lesion is a 1.5 cm raised nodule covered by thick, adherent, yellow-brown crust and scale, firm and indurated at its base, on sun-damaged skin.
brief.task: Interpret the written findings for both lesions. The examiner will then read out the histology findings. Answer questions on risk and management.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Two lesions, two diseases: name each, say how it behaves, then set the margin by risk.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Quoting a 4 mm margin for the nose. The nose is a high-risk site.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "The nose shows a nodular basal cell carcinoma; the scalp lesion looks like a squamous cell carcinoma."

grid.label: Recognises each lesion
grid.fail: Calls both lesions the same, or cannot describe either.
grid.pass: Nose: pearly nodule, rolled edge, fine surface vessels: nodular BCC. Scalp: crusted, keratotic, indurated nodule: cutaneous SCC.
grid.high: Adds that keratoacanthoma cannot be told from SCC clinically, so is treated as SCC; Bowen's disease is SCC in situ.

grid.label: Reads the histology
grid.fail: Cannot name a single histological feature of either tumour.
grid.pass: BCC: nests of basaloid cells with peripheral palisading. SCC: atypical keratinocytes invading the dermis, with keratin pearls.
grid.high: Adds retraction clefts around BCC nests and intercellular bridges in SCC; notes differentiation, depth and perineural invasion should be reported.

grid.label: Behaviour and risk factors
grid.fail: Says BCC and SCC metastasise alike, or cannot give risk factors.
grid.pass: BCC is locally invasive and rarely metastasises; SCC can spread to regional nodes. Risk factors: ultraviolet exposure, fair skin, age, immunosuppression, previous skin cancer.
grid.high: Names features linked to poor SCC outcome: size, depth beyond subcutaneous fat, poor differentiation, perineural invasion, ear or lip site, immunosuppression.

grid.label: Referral urgency
grid.fail: Refers both routinely, or both as suspected cancer.
grid.pass: SCC: consider a suspected cancer pathway referral. BCC: consider non-urgent referral.
grid.high: BCC goes on the suspected cancer pathway only if delay could have a significant impact because of site or size.

grid.label: Examines the nodes
grid.fail: Does not examine the regional nodes for the scalp SCC.
grid.pass: Examines parotid and cervical nodes for the scalp SCC; suspicious nodes need ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration.
grid.high: Would consider high-resolution nodal ultrasound in the clinically node-negative high-risk patient; discusses at the skin cancer MDT.

grid.label: BCC margin
grid.fail: Takes a 4 mm margin from the nose, or quotes melanoma margins.
grid.pass: The nose is a high-risk site: excise with at least a 5 mm peripheral margin. Low-risk BCC: 4 mm.
grid.high: Consider Mohs micrographic surgery for high-risk primary BCC; offer it first line for recurrent high-risk BCC.

grid.label: SCC margin
grid.fail: Cannot give an SCC margin, or uses the same margin whatever the risk.
grid.pass: Peripheral margin by risk: at least 4 mm low risk, 6 mm high risk, 10 mm very high risk.
grid.high: Adds that at least 1 mm histological clearance is the aim; the final risk group depends on the histology report.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: What do the findings suggest for each lesion?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: It's cancer cells in the skin. I'm not sure of the details.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: They both spread to the lymph nodes like melanoma.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: How urgently should her GP have referred her?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: 4 mm, like any basal cell carcinoma.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: What do the findings suggest for each lesion?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: The nose has a pearly nodule with a rolled edge and fine surface vessels: a nodular basal cell carcinoma. The scalp lesion is crusted, keratotic and indurated, so I'd treat it as a squamous cell carcinoma.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: I'll read out the histology. What does it show?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: The first shows nests of basaloid cells with peripheral palisading, which is BCC. The second shows atypical keratinocytes invading the dermis with keratin pearls, which is SCC.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: How do they differ in behaviour?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: BCC is locally invasive and rarely metastasises. SCC can spread to regional nodes. Her risks are sun exposure, fair skin and age; immunosuppression and previous skin cancer also matter.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: How urgently should she have been referred?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: The SCC warrants a suspected cancer pathway referral. For BCC NICE advises non-urgent referral.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: The parotid and neck nodes, because of the scalp SCC. Any suspicious node needs ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: The nose is a high-risk site, so at least 5 mm. A low-risk BCC would be 4 mm.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: It depends on risk: at least 4 mm if low risk, 6 mm if high, 10 mm if very high.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Could the scalp lesion be anything else?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: A keratoacanthoma, but it can't be reliably told from SCC clinically, so I'd excise it as an SCC. Bowen's disease would be SCC in situ, confined to the epidermis.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: What else would you look for in the histology?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Retraction clefts around the BCC nests, and intercellular bridges in the SCC. I'd want the report to give differentiation, depth and any perineural invasion.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Size, invasion beyond subcutaneous fat, poor differentiation, perineural invasion, ear or lip site, and immunosuppression, particularly after organ transplant.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Would a BCC ever go on the suspected cancer pathway?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Yes, if a delay could have a significant impact because of its site or size.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: For a high-risk SCC I'd still consider high-resolution nodal ultrasound, and discuss her at the skin cancer MDT.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Is standard excision the only option for the nose?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Mohs micrographic surgery should be considered for a high-risk primary BCC, and offered first line if it recurs.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I'd aim for at least 1 mm histological clearance, and use the report's depth, differentiation and perineural invasion to confirm the risk group.

failures.move: Taking a 4 mm margin from the nose.
failures.consequence: The nose is a high-risk site; an under-sized margin risks incomplete excision and recurrence in a cosmetically critical area.

failures.move: Treating SCC as locally invasive only, like BCC.
failures.consequence: The nodes go unassessed and nodal spread is found late.

failures.move: Not examining the parotid and neck nodes.
failures.consequence: Misses nodal disease that changes staging and surgery.
Delays treatment of a tumour that can metastasise.

recovery.when: You can't recall the exact SCC margins
recovery.line: The SCC margin scales with risk, and the nose BCC is high risk by site, so neither gets the smallest margin.
A keratotic, indurated scalp nodule is an SCC until histology says otherwise.

knowledge.fact: BCC: pearly nodule, rolled edge, fine vessels; basaloid nests with peripheral palisading.
SCC: keratotic, indurated or ulcerated nodule; invasive atypical keratinocytes with keratin pearls.
NG12: consider a suspected cancer pathway referral for SCC; non-urgent referral for BCC unless site or size makes delay significant.
BCC margins: 4 mm low risk; at least 5 mm with a high-risk factor, such as a central face or nose site.
SCC margins: at least 4, 6 and 10 mm for low, high and very high risk; aim for 1 mm histological clearance.
Suspicious nodes in SCC: ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration.

recall.think: SCC can spread to nodes; a nose BCC can destroy the nose.
recall.say: "Nodular BCC on the nose, SCC on the scalp."
do: Name each lesion and its histology
Set the margin by risk group

numbers.meaning: BCC margin: low risk / high risk
SCC margin: low / high / very high risk

recall.trap: A small nose BCC is still high risk by site.
recall.finish: Excision with the right margin, or Mohs for high-risk BCC; skin cancer MDT.

sources.name: Nasr I, et al. British Association of Dermatologists guidelines for the management of adults with basal cell carcinoma 2021. Br J Dermatol 2021;185:899–920
sources.supports: 4 mm peripheral margin for low-risk BCC (R6); at least 5 mm with a high-risk factor (R7); high-risk sites include the nose and central face; consider Mohs for high-risk primary BCC (R9) and offer it first line for recurrent high-risk BCC (R10)

sources.name: Keohane SG, Botting J, Budny PG, et al. British Association of Dermatologists guidelines for the management of people with cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma 2020. Br J Dermatol 2021;184:401–414
sources.supports: Peripheral margins of at least 4, 6 and 10 mm for low, high and very high-risk cSCC (R6); at least 1 mm histological clearance (R7); risk factors including depth beyond subcutaneous fat and perineural invasion; consider high-resolution nodal ultrasound in the N0 setting; ultrasound-guided FNA for suspicious nodes

partner.opening: Here are the written findings for two lesions from the same patient. Tell me what you think each one is.

reveals.finding: Read out: section from the nasal lesion: the dermis contains rounded nests of small cells with dark oval nuclei and scant cytoplasm. The outermost cells of each nest line up in a regular row, and a thin empty space separates each nest from the surrounding stroma. Section from the scalp lesion: irregular tongues of large cells with abundant pink cytoplasm and enlarged, irregular nuclei extend down from the epidermis into the dermis. Some groups surround concentric whorls of pink keratin, and adjacent cells are joined by fine spiny connections.

reveals.trigger: Candidate asks to examine the nodes
reveals.finding: Read out: no palpable parotid or cervical nodes.
Read out: none. No previous skin cancer.

reveals.trigger: Candidate asks for the SCC histology report
reveals.finding: Read out: Moderately differentiated SCC, 3 mm thick, no perineural invasion; margins to follow excision.

push.question: How do these two tumours behave differently?
push.expect: BCC local invasion, metastasis rare; SCC can spread to nodes.

push.question: How urgently should each be referred?
push.expect: SCC suspected cancer pathway; BCC non-urgent unless site or size makes delay significant.

push.question: What margin for the nose?
push.expect: High-risk site: at least 5 mm, or consider Mohs.

push.question: And for the scalp?
push.expect: At least 4, 6 or 10 mm by risk group.

curveballs.prompt: She has had a kidney transplant.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Immunosuppression raises SCC risk and aggression; treat as higher risk and involve the transplant team and skin cancer MDT.
Autosomal dominant basal cell naevus syndrome: multiple BCCs from a young age, jaw keratocysts and palmar pits.

curveballs.prompt: The scalp lesion grew over a few weeks. Could it be a keratoacanthoma?
curveballs.safeAnswer: Possibly, but it cannot be reliably separated from SCC, so excise and treat as SCC.

curveballs.prompt: The report shows the SCC is excised with a 0.5 mm deep margin.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Below the 1 mm clearance target: discuss at the skin cancer MDT about further treatment.
